chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Abbas ibn Musa from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Ibn Muskhan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding the porter who breaks what he carried or spills it.
He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he is trustworthy (ma'mun), there is no liability upon him; and if he is not trustworthy, he is liable (dhamin).'

key_terms.ضَامِن: Liable / guarantor (one who bears the financial responsibility for loss)
key_terms.مَأْمُون: Trustworthy / reliable (one who is not expected to be negligent)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in liability between a trustworthy and non-trustworthy porter in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In the context of *al-Ijarat* (contracts of hire) in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration clarifies the standard of care for carriers by linking liability to their general reputation for trustworthiness (*ma'mun*) rather than requiring proof of negligence in every instance. This reflects the Shia juristic view that a trustworthy agent is exempt from compensation for ordinary wear and tear or accidental loss, whereas a less reliable carrier bears full risk (*daman*).
